BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Process note:** The Seller's "reviewer efficiency note" asks us to skip every item marked [STANDARD] because both sides have supposedly cleared it. We have not. Nothing in the record shows Wattlebridge accepted these positions, and most [STANDARD] items conflict with the playbook. All 16 items below are reviewed.

**Fallbacks:** Amelia Frost has not given written authority for any fallback. Do not offer the 20% cap (SPA-N-001) or the 18-month period (SPA-N-003) without her written approval identifying the draft.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer should want:** 25%, AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Reason:** The 20% cap is a conditional fallback that requires Amelia Frost's written authority, which has not been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000 with recovery only of the excess (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter.
- **Reason:** A true deductible at these levels would strip out most of the realistic general warranty recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion for general claims (cl 12.3/13). Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months. Limitations apply only to the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at 24 months. Reject the blanket "applies to all Claims" wording.
- **Reason:** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, and the blanket wording would also capture fundamental and fraud claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright.
- **Reason:** Applying general-regime limits to title and capacity fundamentally undermines the ownership protection the buyer is paying for.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). No fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert the carve-out.
- **Reason:** As drafted, the limitation and non-reliance provisions would protect a seller who deliberately conceals material facts.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (to 5.00pm 22 Sept 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public searches (DD 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific, fair disclosure only. No whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Require specific disclosure against each warranty.
- **Reason:** General disclosure would neutralise most warranties, since the buyer cannot reasonably review everything in the data room. Also, the non-admission wording in DD 1.4 should not be used to narrow what counts as a breach.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Buyer has no claim for any matter known to the buyer or its advisers, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and delete.
- **Reason:** "Discoverable" is an unlimited standard that turns the buyer's diligence into a reason to lose claims.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). Disclosure 2 confirms no final written consent and no evidence the conditions are met.
- **Buyer should want:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make effective consent plus condition evidence a condition precedent.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m), and the conditions are currently unmet.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be released after Completion (cl 2/7). Disclosure 3 confirms it has not been repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer should want:** Current payout figures, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Require a payoff letter and direct repayment in the funds flow.
- **Reason:** Leaving a AUD 3.2m secured facility outstanding after Completion exposes the buyer to the lender's security over the company.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow (funds flow note; disclosure 5). On-costs are unquantified.
- **Buyer should want:** A specific funds flow line item or seller funding, including triggered on-costs (payroll tax and superannuation).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the silent exclusion. Require a specific line item or seller funding, with on-costs quantified.
- **Reason:** The bonuses are triggered at Completion, so leaving them outside the funds flow would leave the company with the cost.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (cl 11.1), described as "adequate". Disclosure 4: transfer of SOW3 materials is conditional on payment of all SOW3 fees. AUD 180,000 is open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer should want:** A broadened indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 should be independently verified, neither accepted nor dismissed on the current record.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow indemnity. Broaden it, keep the cure mechanism, and obtain independent verification of the AUD 180,000.
- **Reason:** A payment-only indemnity does not protect against the IP transfer failing for other reasons.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." Disclosure 6: download link sent to an unintended external address; up to ~1,240 records; access, scope and notification obligations unknown.
- **Buyer should want:** Log preservation, investigation, and regular updates from the seller. Treat as no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the materiality characterisation. Require log preservation, a completed investigation, and regular updates. Refer to privacy counsel to assess notification obligations.
- **Reason:** The seller cannot yet establish scope or access, so it cannot credibly call the matter immaterial.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, described as ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure 8 does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer should want:** Assessment of the contracts and their terms. No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Assess. Request the contracts and timing, and hold for the debt and working capital review.
- **Reason:** The current record does not support either a debt classification or a price deduction.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Title, tax, IP and warranty categories are merged under the general regime, and all limitations apply to all claims.
- **Buyer should want:** Title, tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Restore separate regimes.
- **Reason:** Merging the categories lets the general cap and time limits override the protections for fundamental and tax/IP issues.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the company share register at DD-012 (cl and disclosure 10).
- **Buyer should want:** Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Require independent verification before Completion. Examples: an ASIC company extract, PPSR searches, a share transfer and board authority, and confirmation of no encumbrances over the shares.
- **Reason:** The seller's own register cannot verify its own title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP terms remain open. No unlimited liability and no resolution assumed.
- **Recommendation:** Keep open. Do not accept the seller's "settled" characterisation.
- **Reason:** The playbook treats these as unresolved, and the seller's proposal is the general regime that we are rejecting.

---

**Summary of decisions needed:**
- Amelia Frost's written authority is required before any fallback on SPA-N-001 or SPA-N-003 is offered.
- Diligence requests: Sandbar contracts (N-013), Ironquay verification of AUD 180k (N-011), Bluefen consent and conditions (N-008), Riverlark payoff letter (N-009), independent title evidence (N-015), export incident logs and investigation (N-012).
